newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil ends lower in Europe, softs par losses.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil ends lower in Europe, softs par losses.

text.p: Palm oil prices finished lower in Europe on Tuesday partly on the back of a lower Malaysian close and a poor outlook for exports.
Figures released by Malaysian cargo surveyor Societe General de Surveillance (SGS) contained no surprises and had little impact on the market.
SGS said it estimated Malaysia's palm oil exports for February 1-25 at 360,382 tonnes against 401,932 in January 1-25.
Traders said the future trend in palm oil would depend very much on exports, but with India not buying much the market seemed to be heading for a downturn.
"The SGS figures show Pakistan as the main buyer, but next to nothing going to India, which isn't good,' said one trader.
Soft oils pared early losses after Chicago soy oil futures rallied following a lower opening.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $2.50 to $7.50 down after March traded at $567.50 and April/June at $555 a tonne cif.
Products finished with RBD oil $2.50 lower while olein was unchanged and stearin $2.50 to $7.50 down on the day.
Traders said one or two additional trades were reported during the afternoon, but they did not amount to much.
Coconut oil closed $5 down to unchanged after Jan/Feb traded at $777.50, Feb/Mar at $772.50 and Mar/Apr at $762.50 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil was unchanged after Feb/Mar traded at $755 a tonne cif.
Dutch soy oil closed unchanged while rape oil was unchanged to 0.50 guilders lower.
March soy oil fetched 98 and 98.50 guilders while 100 guilders was paid for May/Jul and 101 for Aug/Oct.
Rape oil traded at 100 guilders for May/Jul and 100.50 for Aug/Oct.
However, traders said the tonnage traded was not high.
